status_note: Pre-simulation 2D hydrodynamic case-study benchmark & scenario framework (LISFLOOD-FP / BASEMENT target) — screening-resolution ~90 m 2D inertial simulation available in data/tsho_rolpa_2d_inundation.json, but NOT yet a 2D inundation map of design-grade engineering fidelity (awaiting <=5 m LiDAR/UAV DEM)

lake_identification.name: Tsho Rolpa
lake_identification.river_basin: Rolwaling Khola → Tama Koshi → Sun Koshi (Saptakoshi)

bathymetry_and_geometry.historical_expansion_note: Expanded from ~0.23 km2 (1957-1959 Survey of India / aerial photography) to ~1.53-1.65 km2 in 1990s-2010s surveys and ~1.66 km2 in TRĀYA inventory.

comparison_with_traya_empirical_scaling.depth_check: Surveyed max depth 132 m falls comfortably inside TRĀYA Veh et al. (2020) 95% interval [46, 335] m (median 122 m).
comparison_with_traya_empirical_scaling.volume_bias_note: TRĀYA half-ellipsoid volume (135.72 Mm3) overestimates surveyed bathymetric volume (76-86 Mm3) by ~1.6-1.8x because real moraine-dammed basins are shallower near shorelines than an ideal half-ellipsoid. 2D hydrodynamic simulations MUST use surveyed bathymetry rather than half-ellipsoid volume.

citations: Yamada, T. (1998), Glacier Lake and its Outburst Flood in the Nepal Himalaya, Data Center for Glacier Research, Japanese Society of Snow and Ice, Monograph 1.
Reynolds, J.M. (1999), Glacial hazard assessment at Tsho Rolpa, Rolwaling, Central Nepal, Q. J. Eng. Geol. 32(3), 209-214.
ICIMOD (2011), Glacial Lakes and Glacial Lake Outburst Floods in Nepal, Kathmandu.
Shrestha, B.B., Nakagawa, H. (2014), Assessment of potential outburst floods from the Tsho Rolpa glacial lake in Nepal, Natural Hazards 73, 1119-1139, doi:10.1007/s11069-013-0940-3.

engineering_mitigation_2000.intervention: 3.0 m artificial lake-level lowering via open gated spillway channel
engineering_mitigation_2000.implementing_agencies: Nepal DHM / WECS with Netherlands Government & Reynolds Geo-Sciences support
engineering_mitigation_2000.residual_risk_note: Lowering the lake by 3 m reduced hydrostatic pressure and storage by ~4-5 Mm3, but the terminal moraine remains ice-cored with steep distal slopes (SLA = 17.5-21.8 deg) and ~76-86 Mm3 retained volume; full 15-20 m lowering proposed in Phase II was never constructed.
citations: Damen, M. (1992), Study on the potential outburst flooding of Tsho Rolpa glacier lake, Rolwaling Valley, East Nepal, ITC Enschede report.

Rana, B., Shrestha, A.B., Reynolds, J.M., Aryal, R., Pokhrel, A.P., Budhathoki, K.P. (2000), Hazard assessment of the Tsho Rolpa Glacier Lake and ongoing remediation measures, J. Nepal Geol. Soc. 22, 563-570.

nearby_historical_glofs_25km.driver: overflow water from Upper Ngole Cho

valley_checkpoints.name: Na
valley_checkpoints.significance: First inhabited alpine settlement below Tsho Rolpa terminal moraine; high-energy near-field debris/surge impact zone with minimal lead time.

valley_checkpoints.name: Beding
valley_checkpoints.significance: Main Rolwaling Sherpa village (~12 km downstream); previously impacted by the 1991 Chubung GLOF and dependent on single valley trail/bridge egress.

valley_checkpoints.name: Gongar (Gonggar)
valley_checkpoints.significance: Tama Koshi valley floor immediately below the Chetchet confluence (28.8 km); hosts NH28 / F106 vehicular river bridges and the Upper Tamakoshi HPP powerhouse/tailrace complex.

valley_checkpoints.name: Upper Tamakoshi HPP (456 MW)
valley_checkpoints.valley_reach: Tama Koshi — Gongar Tailrace/Powerhouse & Lamabagar Headworks
valley_checkpoints.significance: Nepal's largest operating hydropower plant (456 MW). Note on spatial geometry: the OSM plant polygon tags the Lamabagar headworks dam (~5.8 km upstream of the Rolwaling confluence on the Tama Koshi mainstem), whereas the underground powerhouse portal, tailrace outfall, switchyard, and access road lie directly on the Tsho Rolpa GLOF corridor at Gongar (~31.6 km downstream) and require 2D tailrace-backwater & sediment modelling.

valley_checkpoints.name: Singati (Town, Bridge & Community Hospital)
valley_checkpoints.significance: Major commercial, road-bridge (Singati Bridge at 46.2 km), and healthcare node (Singati Community Hospital at 46.6 km); loss of Singati crossing severs upper Dolakha / Rolwaling emergency hospital access.

valley_checkpoints.name: Dolakha (Tamakoshi Bazar / NH23 Bridge Corridor)
valley_checkpoints.valley_reach: Lower-Middle Tama Koshi (Dolakha HQ Valley Floor)
valley_checkpoints.significance: Primary NH23 arterial bridge & valley-floor hospital corridor serving Charikot / Dolakha district headquarters (situated upslope above Tama Koshi gorge).

valley_checkpoints.name: Khimti (Tama Koshi–Khimti Confluence)
valley_checkpoints.significance: Valley settlement and NH28 crossings near the Khimti I (60 MW) hydropower corridor.

valley_checkpoints.name: Manthali
valley_checkpoints.significance: Ramechhap district headquarters, riverfront airport, and regional road junction.

valley_checkpoints.name: Khurkot (Sun Koshi Confluence & BP Highway)
valley_checkpoints.significance: Confluence of Tama Koshi with Sun Koshi and strategic BP Highway (NH03) trunk bridge linking Kathmandu Valley to eastern Nepal; far-field attenuated surge checkpoint (~103 km).

breach_scenario_framework.label: Minor / Spillway-Notch Partial Breach (10% depth fraction)
breach_scenario_framework.published_analog: Post-2000 lowered-spillway partial erosion / ~10-15 m overtopping breach
breach_scenario_framework.target_2d_solver_role: Baseline serviceability & bridge freeboard check (LISFLOOD-FP / BASEMENT)

breach_scenario_framework.label: Moderate Moraine-Dam Breach (30% depth fraction)
breach_scenario_framework.published_analog: Shrestha & Nakagawa (2014) 20-30 m moraine-dam breach benchmark (~30-35 Mm3 drained)
breach_scenario_framework.target_2d_solver_role: Primary design-basis GLOF hydrograph for Rolwaling–Gongar–Singati floodplain zoning

breach_scenario_framework.label: Severe Ice-Cored Moraine Collapse (50% depth fraction)
breach_scenario_framework.published_analog: High-impact avalanche + ice-cored moraine incision (~50-65 m lowering, approaching Fujita Hp=66.6 m)
breach_scenario_framework.target_2d_solver_role: Upper-bound evacuation planning & Upper Tamakoshi tailrace backwater stress test

breach_scenario_framework.label: Extreme Full-Depth Bounding Case (100% depth fraction)
breach_scenario_framework.published_analog: Physical bounding envelope only (full bathymetric drainage is geomorphically unlikely)
breach_scenario_framework.target_2d_solver_role: Sensitivity ceiling only — NOT a probable operational scenario

simulation_2d_summary.methodology_notice: Screening-resolution 2D inertial shallow-water simulation (Bates et al., 2010 / LISFLOOD-FP formulation) on ESA Copernicus DEM GLO-30 (~90 m thalweg-preserving grid) — awaiting <=5 m LiDAR/UAV bare-earth DEM for engineering design & statutory zoning
simulation_2d_summary.solver_formulation: Bates et al. (2010) 2D inertial shallow-water (LISFLOOD-FP formulation)

required_inputs_for_lisflood_basement: High-resolution <=2-5 m bare-earth DEM (UAV photogrammetry / airborne LiDAR / Pleiades stereo) of the Rolwaling gorge and Tama Koshi floodplains
Updated multi-beam / sonar bathymetry of Tsho Rolpa (post-2020 ice-front retreat & lake expansion)
Moraine geotechnical & ice-core ERT/GPR cross-sections for physical breach-erosion parameterization (BASEMENT / BREACH)
Two-phase hyperconcentrated / debris-flow rheology parameters (entrainment & bulking along steep Rolwaling reaches)
Calibrated Manning's n roughness across alpine boulder channels, forested gorges, and Tama Koshi bridge constrictions
As-built deck elevation & abutment clearances for Gongar, Singati Bridge, NH28/NH23 bridges, and Upper Tamakoshi tailrace outfall
current_traya_screening_limitations: 1 km corridor around HydroRIVERS/DEM thalweg is a screening search zone — NOT a 2D inundation boundary
Arrival times use first-order surge-front velocities (2 / 5 / 10 m/s) without channel-storage attenuation or debris bulking
No site-specific flood depth, flow velocity, shear stress, or bridge scour is computed yet
